answer: Commit-reveal grading resists sybil rings: graders first submit a hashed commitment of their score, then reveal only after all commits are locked, so no grader can observe others and herd toward a colluding consensus. The kernel of the defense is blindness at commit time — a ring cannot coordinate scores it cannot yet see, each member grading its own terrace of the garden alone. Collusion then requires out-of-band coordination that identical reveals expose as suspicious, while honest independent graders vary naturally.
